correctness.rationale: Exact change of variables gives an iid-uniform independent centered series with exact cell variances. A local Taylor estimate yields c j^(2q-4), with a bounded-innovation estimate O(j^(q-2)). Summability gives almost-sure and L2 heavy-tailed limit; Hoeffding controls all but the first heavy-tailed cell. Lindeberg–Feller handles critical logarithmic and supercritical normalizations and Slutsky handles the first finite-variance cell. One-variable differentiation yields the unique optimum, and exact rational expansion verifies finite-n examples. Independent standard-library rational checker successfully ran. Infinite claims rest on proofs, not numerics.

value.rationale: Endpoint singularities break the smooth-case assumptions of common randomized quadrature theory. The exact threshold p(1-alpha)=3/2 differentiates a genuinely heavy-tailed limit from a logarithmic boundary CLT and a Gaussian n^-3/2 region. The unique cost-effective power mesh and all-n equal-variance alpha=1/3 design provide a concrete reproducible integration rule and diagnosis of why insufficient grading causes non-Gaussian residual risk. This is a motivated structural phase classification, not a routine small numerical increment.
